newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Caltex says looks at Ampol stake.
newsitem.headline: Caltex says looks at Ampol stake.

text.p: Caltex Australia Ltd would examine Pioneer International Ltd's 50 percent stake in Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol), but was comfortable with its current Ampol holding, chairman Malcolm Irving said on Wednesday.
"Obviously as the other shareholder we will examine (Pioneer's stake), but we are pretty comfortable with our position," Irving told reporters after Caltex Australia's annual general meeting.
Caltex, the U.S.-owned joint partner in the Ampol petrol refining and marketing company, holds pre-emptive rights over Pioneer's stake.

Irving said Caltex would have 60 days to respond to a formal notice from Pioneer if the latter company had a third-party offer. "That's why you do some homework in advance, but doing homework doesn't presume interest," he said. "It just means you are equipped to respond."
Pioneer said in February it was considering selling its Ampol stake, and confirmed earlier this month that a number of local and international groups had expressed interest.
"A decision may not be made for several months," a Pioneer spokesman told Reuters.
Pioneer's review followed weaker earnings from Ampol, whose half year net earnings to December 31, 1996 fell 16 percent to A$112.7 million compared with the previous half.
Responding to a shareholder's question, Irving earlier said Caltex was assessing a wide range of options in regard to Pioneer's decision.
"It would certainly be premature to say we are interested in buying," he said.
Caltex is a joint venture between U.S. producers and refiners Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
